diagnostic_evidence.quote: By taking expectation on \eqref{mul-ide-1}-\eqref{mul-ide-2}, we have that

issues.failure_explanation: The phase of û(t2)/û(t1) contains the term Σ_odd b_β(iξ)^β (W(t2)−W(t1)). This increment is Gaussian and unbounded, with variance t2−t1, and the factor |ξ|^{|β|} is arbitrarily large over the modes used. Hence for any t2−t1>0 the phase leaves (−π,π] with positive probability, and the principal Arg is wrapped. E[Arg(·)] then does not equal the drift sum, because the zero-mean W-term does not average out after wrapping. Identity (dri-mul-ide2) fails. Also, Arg is applied to an absolute value, which has no argument. The statement that the parameters are determined by 'the solution at two time points' hides that the argument needs expectations over many paths.

failure_location.quote: Notice that for $|t_2-t_1|>0$ sufficiently small, the phase ambiguity in \eqref{mul-ide-2} can be removed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Avoid taking the expectation of the wrapped phase. Work with E of the complex ratio, i.e. E û(t2)/E û(t1) as in the additive case, using E[e^{cΔW}]=e^{c²Δt/2}. Alternatively, state an explicit bound on the increment under which no wrapping occurs.
issues.overall_effect: Identification of the odd-order drift coefficients in the multiplicative-noise case is not established. The even-order part, via E log|·|, is unaffected.
issues.title: Expectation of wrapped Arg and removal of phase ambiguity is invalid in the multiplicative case
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument using the complex ratio of expectations fixes the odd part without changing the result's scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose that $\mathcal Q_1$ is not located on an algebraic polynomial hypersurface of degree $\le 2p_2$ consisting of only even-order terms.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrices A_even and A_odd in the proof have columns ξ^γ with |γ| ≤ 2p_2, i.e. they involve the diffusion order p_2. Full column rank therefore requires Q_1 to avoid hypersurfaces of degree ≤ 2p_2. The stated condition is in terms of the drift order p_1, and 'sufficiently large' is never quantified in the theorem. If p_2>p_1, the stated hypothesis does not give full rank.

V_2 is built from resolvents applied to the random function e^{𝓛t/2+𝒢W(t)}u_0. Separately, Σ_{k≤M}E|c_k|² is wrongly bounded by the tail bound θ²M^{1-2γ}/(2γ-1), although the partial sum is O(1).

issues.failure_explanation: G is a function of (s,t), but the proof argues differentiability in x. The C^p regularity of G(s,t) in the time variables is needed for λ_j=o(j^{-(p+1)}) and is not proved. Brownian time-dependence typically destroys it: for u_0=cos x, c≡1 one gets u=cos(x−W_t) and G(s,t)=πe^{-|t−s|/2}, which has a kink on the diagonal. Its eigenvalues decay only like j^{-2}, whatever p is. Moreover G has the expectation inside, so it is not the kernel whose spectrum equals that of K. In the example K has rank 2 while G has infinite rank. The displayed identity equating the K-projection error with the G-tail sum is therefore false.

issues.failure_explanation: Conclusions 1 and 2 concern global optimal values and the global argmin sets Ψ_N, Ψ_O. The hypothesis is only that some k-sparse point is a local minimizer, and no boundedness or level-compactness of minimizers is assumed. Epi-convergence-type results on optimal values and limsup of argmin sets require global conditions such as inf-compactness or uniform boundedness. Pointwise SLLN convergence alone is insufficient, and the set C_k is also mis-defined with ‖c‖ instead of ‖c‖_0.

issues.failure_explanation: Small p-values (non-Gaussianity) correspond to Z_N very negative, so a two-sided |Z_N| test is wrong: large positive Z_N means p-values near 1 and is not evidence of multiplicative noise. For p*<1/2, Φ^{-1}(p*)<0, so the first condition always holds and the second never does. For p*>1/2 the two thresholds Φ^{-1}(p*) and Φ^{-1}(p*)/2 leave an undefined gap. The factor 2 is unjustified, and the significance level does not control the false-positive rate. Gaussianity of the residuals under additive noise also ignores the O(Δt^{3/2}) drift bias and the O(Δt)-scale drift error.
